titre: Sex Chromosomes Were Not Discovered by Morgan
accroche: In 1905, two researchers separately discover the sex chromosomes, yet neither of their names is the one most often cited
contenu_vulgarise:
In the spring of 1905, at Bryn Mawr College, Nettie Stevens observes under the microscope the reproductive cells of *Tenebrio molitor*, the mealworm beetle. She counts the chromosomes, one by one, in reproductive cells and in body cells.

In males, she finds nineteen large chromosomes and a twentieth, distinctly smaller. In females, all twenty chromosomes are large, without exception: the total number is the same, and it is the size of one chromosome that changes. Half of the sperm carry the small chromosome, the other half do not.

Stevens draws a cautious but clear conclusion: an egg fertilized by a sperm carrying the small chromosome becomes a male; the other becomes a female. She adds that the small chromosome may not itself be what determines sex, but that sex may, in some cases, depend on a difference in the quantity or quality of chromatin between sperm. Sex can be read in a difference between chromosomes that is visible under the microscope, not in an invisible, hypothetical factor.

## A discovery by two, almost simultaneous

The same year, a few months earlier, Edmund Wilson, already an established professor at Columbia, publishes a study of the sex chromosomes of hemipterans, insects such as true bugs. He shows that males possess an unequal pair of chromosomes, whose smaller member he names the idiochromosome. The two researchers do not work together, but they cite each other: Wilson adds a note to his paper pointing out that Stevens independently found, in a beetle, an unequal pair of chromosomes similar to his idiochromosomes, and Stevens mentions in a footnote that Wilson observed a similar dimorphism in the sperm of other hemipterans.

Neither of them presented their reading as definitive. Wilson nevertheless judges that Stevens’s discovery strongly supports McClung’s hypothesis, according to which a particular chromosome is linked to sex, and that it may eventually prove well founded. It is the convergence of two independent observations, on different insects, that gives the chromosomal hypothesis of sex its strength.

## The name that stays, and the one that fades

Thomas Hunt Morgan supervised Stevens’s doctoral thesis at Bryn Mawr, and he is the name most readers associate today with the genetics of the early century: Nobel Prize in 1933, for establishing the chromosome theory of heredity, work carried out later on the fruit fly.

Yet the 1905 episode does not belong to him: at the time, Morgan was not in favor of McClung’s suggestion of 1901-1902, he did not accept the results of Stevens and Wilson without reservation, and he would not come around to the idea that chromosomes carry heredity until shortly after 1910, under the weight of growing experimental evidence. The credit for the discovery is shared between Stevens and Wilson. Wilson published a few months earlier, but some attribute it to Stevens because her conclusions were firmer; her 1905 monograph was nonetheless cited fewer than a hundred times in 2021, according to Google Scholar.

A founding discovery does not need a single discoverer to be sound. What it does need is that the story told about it does not invent one.

repere.texte: In Tenebrio molitor, Nettie Stevens counts twenty chromosomes in the female, all large, versus nineteen large and one small in the male. She publishes this result in 1905, the same year as Edmund Wilson on other insects; her monograph was cited fewer than a hundred times in 2021 (Google Scholar, according to the authors).
repere.source: Carey, Aközbek & Harkess, “The contributions of Nettie Stevens to the field of sex chromosome biology,” Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 377, 2022

carte.punch: Sex chromosomes were not discovered by the man whose name you remember.
carte.idee: In 1905, Nettie Stevens and Edmund Wilson independently observed, in different insects, an unequal pair of chromosomes linked to sex. Morgan, whom we associate with this period, was not the discoverer: he supervised Stevens’s thesis and came around only after 1910.
carte.source_courte: Carey et al., Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B, 2022

quiz.question: What does Nettie Stevens observe in Tenebrio molitor in 1905 when she compares males and females?
choix: A distinctly smaller chromosome in the male, for the same total number
A chromosome entirely missing in the male, with no replacement
No visible difference between the chromosomes of the two sexes
An extra chromosome in the female, absent in the male
quiz.explication: In Tenebrio, male and female both have twenty chromosomes: the female twenty large ones, the male nineteen large and one small. Stevens concludes that an egg fertilized by a sperm carrying the small chromosome becomes a male. Morgan, for his part, would not accept the idea that chromosomes carry heredity until shortly after 1910.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In the note added to his 1905 paper on hemipterans, what does Edmund Wilson say about Nettie Stevens’s results?
choix: She independently found, in a beetle, an unequal pair of chromosomes similar to his own
She reproduced his own results on hemipterans before he had even published them
She showed that chromosomes have nothing to do with sex in insects
She counted one fewer chromosome in the female Tenebrio than in the male
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Wilson adds that Stevens independently discovered in Tenebrio an unequal pair of chromosomes similar to his idiochromosomes, and that these results strongly support McClung’s hypothesis.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does the Nobel Prize awarded to Morgan in 1933 not reward the 1905 discovery of the sex chromosomes?
choix: Because Morgan discovered the sex chromosomes alone, without Stevens or Wilson
Because it rewards a separate and later body of work: the chromosome theory of heredity, established on the fruit fly
Because the Nobel committee judged the 1905 discovery not reproducible
Because Morgan published his own discovery before Stevens and Wilson, as early as 1903
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 1933 Nobel rewards the establishment of the chromosome theory of heredity, carried out later on Drosophila, work distinct from the 1905 discovery.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What role did Thomas Hunt Morgan play for Nettie Stevens before the 1905 discovery?
choix: He co-signed with her the 1905 monograph on Tenebrio molitor
He succeeded her as a professor at the Carnegie Institution
He funded her research with a personal grant
He supervised her doctoral thesis at Bryn Mawr
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Morgan supervised Stevens’s thesis at Bryn Mawr; he himself accepted the idea that chromosomes carry heredity only shortly after 1910.
